what: the sources the language admission struck on our own label, back on what each one's own source says it is. The language admission (language-admission-rule-v1) judged a source by the label this project gave it; its record says of every source it struck for silence that «the fix is a label at the source naming what its own title page names, not an exception here». The corpus lane's relay v210 corrects its relay v207: the owner never repealed the language ban of 31 August for a defining source (an M stays Hebrew and Aramaic only), and the source ledger is reissued as v1.1, which judges three labels row by row (BY_ROW), each row by its own source's language field. Of those, English Wiktionary's translation tables return now, for the rows the ledger admits and no other. Their index entry is the one the store held before the strike, with the languages its own source names and no wording year. The rows themselves land by the landings' rule (data/landings/PIN.json).
